⚡ Your energy bill goes up £60 on 1 October.

But here's the bit buried in Ofgem's notes to editors that nobody reads 👇

The cap is quoted as £1,723. On the measuring stick Ofgem used until July, the very same cap would read £1,935.

Why the change? Ofgem now assumes households use 17% less gas than before. And one of the reasons it gives for that fall is, in its own words, "higher prices".

People aren't using less gas because they've become efficient. Plenty are using less because they're frightened of the bill. Heating one room. Going to bed early in February.

That's not progress. That's rationing — and we've quietly baked it into the yardstick. 📉

To be fair to Ofgem: they published both numbers openly. But the honest question is why our energy is this expensive in the first place.

My full piece 👉 https://lukeparker.co.uk/articles/ofgem-tdcv-change-1723-not-1935-september-2026.html
